reviewRationale: The position is approved for a hidden hold-draw technical pilot with an objective correction. The exact tablebase evidence confirms that the initial position is drawn and that every legal initial learner move preserves the draw. Therefore, the exercise must not claim that a3 is the only drawing move or that alternative moves are chess mistakes. The original description of repeated opposition and key-square denial is not sufficiently demonstrated by the approved line. The white king remains on e4 while the white rook pawn advances and is captured on a6. The approved instructional mission is therefore draw preservation through safe rook-pawn liquidation. The authored deterministic line is 1.a3 Kd6 2.a4 Kc5 3.a5 Kb5 4.a6 Kxa6. Success requires the exact terminal with only both kings remaining and insufficient material. Preserving the draw after a single move is not sufficient for success because every legal initial move already does so. Legal moves that preserve the draw but leave the approved route must be described truthfully as objective-miss-result-preserved or authored-concept-miss, never as chess-result-failure. Chess-result-failure applies only when exact evidence shows that the learner draw becomes a loss. The opponent policy may use only authored replies that preserve the theoretical draw. Promotion and stalemate are not approved success conditions. Repetition, uncovered states, integrity failures, and unsafe classifications are technical-unavailable and always neutral. The maximum length is ten plies. The third-stage move reveal removes independent-success eligibility. No result may create persistent scoring, Personal Best, leaderboard data, Training Memory, Mastery, Recommendations, account data, analytics, telemetry, or browser persistence. This approval is bound to the reviewed position, graph, engine evidence, and packet digests. Any change requires a new human-review revision.
